description: Three-panel composite figure (mixed modality) mapping deformation of the hetero-structured Zr0.50 steel; the panels share one field of view, linked by magenta arrows. (a) is a greyscale EBSD image-quality (IQ) map labelled "Global strain = 0%" with blue annotations "Fine FCC" over dark, elongated grain bands and "Coarse FCC" over lighter equiaxed grains, i.e. a bimodal FCC grain structure; a 20 μm scale bar sits at bottom right. (b) and (c) are von Mises local-strain maps (quasi in-situ μ-DIC) of the identical area labelled "Global strain = 2%" and "Global strain = 8%", each with a 20 μm scale bar and a rainbow colour bar whose only printed values are 0 and 12 (unit not printed). At 2 % the high-value red/yellow/orange patches occupy coarse FCC grain interiors and the FG/CG hetero-interfaces, whereas the positions of the fine-FCC bands remain blue/cyan; at 8 % these same bands acquire intermediate green/yellow values while coarse-grain regions stay red. Dark grey streaks (unindexed/particle regions) persist at identical positions in all three panels. The figure demonstrates that strain partitioning between soft CG and hard FG zones exists at 2 % global strain and persists at 8 %.

subfigures.description: Greyscale EBSD image-quality (IQ) map of the unstrained area, labelled 'Global strain = 0%', annotated 'Fine FCC' on dark elongated bands and 'Coarse FCC' on the lighter equiaxed grains; 20 μm scale bar at bottom right.

Coloured von Mises strain map of the same area at 'Global strain = 2%' with a 20 μm scale bar and a rainbow colour bar printed 0 and 12; highest (red/yellow) values lie in coarse FCC grains and along FG/CG interfaces, fine-FCC band locations are low (blue/cyan).

Coloured von Mises strain map at 'Global strain = 8%' with 20 μm scale bar and the same 0–12 colour bar; the fine-FCC regions now show intermediate green/yellow strain while coarse-grain regions remain at high red values.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a greyscale EBSD image-quality map labelled 'Global strain = 0%' containing the blue text annotations 'Fine FCC' (dark elongated bands) and 'Coarse FCC' (lighter equiaxed grains), with a 20 μm scale bar.
Panels (b) and (c) are colour-coded von Mises strain maps of the same field of view, labelled 'Global strain = 2%' and 'Global strain = 8%' respectively, each carrying a 20 μm scale bar.
Both strain maps use a rainbow colour bar whose only printed end labels are 0 and 12; no unit is printed on the colour bar.
Magenta arrows point from (a) to (b) and from (b) to (c), indicating the panels correspond to the same area at increasing global strain.

In (b) the high-value red/orange/yellow patches are located in the coarse FCC grains and on the interfaces between the fine and coarse FCC zones, while the locations of the dark fine-FCC bands remain blue/cyan.
In (c) the fine-FCC regions that were blue/cyan at 2 % now appear green/yellow, i.e. intermediate on the 0–12 scale, while the coarse-grain regions remain red/high.
Dark grey streak-like features occupy identical positions in (a), (b) and (c).
The caption states that (a) is an EBSD-IQ map of the Zr0.50 steel without global strain showing FG and CG zones.
The caption states that (b) and (c) are von Mises strain maps at 2 % and 8 % global strain, respectively, revealing strain partitioning between FG and CG zones.
The citing text states the von Mises maps were obtained from quasi in-situ μ-DIC as a function of global strain.
The citing text states that at a minor plastic strain of 2 % the CG zones and the hetero-interfaces between FG and CG zones experience high strain while the FG zones remain nearly undeformed.
The citing text attributes the partitioning to hardness differences, with CG zones soft and FG zones hard.
The citing text states that at 8 % global strain the local strain of the FG zones becomes more pronounced, so strain partitioning between soft and hard regions persists during plastic deformation.
The citing text states that this strain partitioning generates geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and promotes heterogeneous deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening.
